result.title: Distractor-Robust Reinforcement Learning via Variational Bisimulation
result.summary: Model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) promises data efficiency and generalization, but typical reconstruction-based objectives encourage models to waste representational capacity on task-irrelevant distractors. We introduce VIBES (Variational Inference for Bisimulation-based Encoded States), a new objective that replaces pixel reconstruction with an adversarial term, which enforces that latent states suffice to predict both rewards and the next latent state. We show that this objective measures how far the encoder is from reward and dynamics sufficiency, and that whenever exact sufficiency is attainable, its global optima induce bisimulation relations on histories. Combined with a fixed-capacity latent bottleneck, this encourages latent states to retain task-relevant information while discarding irrelevant variation. Our method serves as a drop-in replacement for Dreamer's model-learning component, achieves state-of-the-art performance on the Distracting Control Suite, and extends to visually complex manipulation in Realistic ManiSkill. Unlike prior approaches, it does not rely on image-specific augmentations and applies equally well to high-dimensional vector-state tasks, demonstrated on a 100-link swimmer robot. Finally, latent-space analyses (UMAP embeddings and nearest-neighbor probes) confirm that the learned representations are sensitive to task-relevant structure while invariant to distractors.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 VIBES：用对抗式目标替代像素重建，约束 latent 状态足以预测奖励与下一 latent 状态，并结合固定容量瓶颈，使 Dreamer 式世界模型的表示保留任务相关信息、忽略干扰物。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「奖励与动力学充分性」加信息瓶颈的度量思路，可能为核查 LVR 内部状态是否保留任务必要视觉信息、如何抑制干扰与信息坍缩提供可借用的训练目标与探针设计。
